From an approved payment
to complete, useful work.

TokenJunkieLabs requests USD 38,000 equivalent in XLM for 400 prospective delivery hours over 150 days from actual award acceptance. The work installs a useful paid Stellar service with two independently operated merchants, two independent buyer operators and the same selected operation through two independently operated facilitators.

The product is open-source, self-hostable merchant and buyer tooling. It carries an approved API request, dataset or paid MCP tool through native settlement, complete useful output, fulfillment and operating handover. The merchant controls its source and terms. The buyer controls its keys, request and spending. Another engineer can reopen the installation and recover unfinished work.

The working development baseline comprises 18 distinct team-operated purchases totaling 411,000 stroops, or 0.0411 native testnet XLM, with network fees recorded separately. The funded milestones establish independent customer operation, repeated use and production receiving from that baseline.

Project and requested outcome

TokenJunkieLabs is building open-source, self-hostable software that connects a useful paid API, dataset or agent operation to the customer's completed work. A merchant publishes an authorized resource. Its buyer approves a particular request and total spending limit, pays through Stellar and receives the complete result in an existing application. The merchant retains the original offer, fulfillment and accounting. Another engineer can reopen the same source, payment and customer output after interruption or handover.

We request $38,000 for 400 prospective delivery hours over 150 days from actual award acceptance. The outcome is two independently operated merchant services serving two independent buyer operators. Both services will be installed by day 30, used recurrently on testnet by day 90, and operated on mainnet with working recovery and maintainer handover by day 150. T2 also operates the same useful service through two independently operated testnet facilitators.

The working product supplies the defined architecture, native payments and complete source-to-customer receiving foundation. The award funds the remaining customer-specific source and receiving adaptations, independent deployment, monitoring and recovery needed by the selected services. Reusable changes return to the public product. The six priced packages below connect that remaining engineering to concrete customer acceptance and recurring use.

Customer problem, need and adoption

Our first customer is a recurring API or data-service operator, or the agency implementing that service in a customer's application. The commissioning payer buys implementation and handover; the independent buyer pays for the useful resource. They may be different organizations. The merchant needs a maintainable service and a clear connection between its offer, accepted output and receipts. The buyer needs the full agreed result, its source meaning and total cost.

For an analyst, a useful result preserves the entire selected population, original units and time basis, and opens as a report or editable data. For an agent application, every required paid page or file must fit the approved task budget. The two supported installation patterns give the selected buyers concrete recurring work:

Installation patternRecurring customer taskAcceptance in the customer's application
A merchant publishes a reviewed economic or operational report.Acquire an agreed new reporting period or source edition, then compare it with the prior result.The complete report and selected underlying data reopen with their units, periods, source edition and review decisions.
A merchant sells a typed dataset or saved query.Acquire a distinct approved query or refreshed population, including all agreed paid pages and files.The complete result reopens with its original request, source selection, aggregate cost and merchant records.

Each installation begins with one workorder naming the commissioning payer, merchant, independent buyer, receiving engineer, authorized source, host and acceptance owner. It fixes the population, period or query, expected output, advertised paid unit and aggregate spending limit before purchase. The first installed execution establishes the operating baseline. New agreed periods, editions or useful queries supply repeat work. The receiving engineer performs an actual source change or recovery before handover. These same tasks continue through the T2 and T3 purchase windows.

The two funded installations and customer agreements remain to be selected. Current conversations establish practical selection conditions: Veridex invited the existing buyer CLI into its testnet cohort and reported no third-party testing budget; CoCart's founder asked who introduces, pays and contracts for customer work; Blockscout expressed interest and reported no integration budget; Nansen declined. The customer and commercial plan retains those original conversations and proposed workshares. Selection must establish an authorized source, accountable operators, useful recurring demand, a receiving host and responsibility for implementation and purchase costs.

Existing source and receiving applications support both patterns. A Timescale customer can receive the original commissioning population, reviewed field/time/quality meanings and baseline-to-observed comparison in an analytical workspace. An aid-data customer can receive selected organisation and activity portfolios with their financial result, original document links, dated acquisition and named source review. These are candidate applications of the delivered architecture; the selected customer's source and responsibilities determine the remaining adaptation.

The maintained scientific-array workflow applies the same commissioning pattern to an explicitly selected time/geographic population. Each variable retains its native type, original indices, units and coordinate arrays through review, publication and customer receiving. Its original operation retained forty upstream arrays and independently reopened the complete source workspace. Brightband's existing ExtremeWeatherBench comparison and proposed $7,200 / ten-business-day workshare remain with their scientific and company owners. Selected installation work joins the approved output to the publisher and customer application, then implements changed-edition operation and another engineer's receiving within the existing packages.

The prepared GeoRobotix Connected Systems workshare is another concrete commercial candidate: one civil or environmental observation source, complete acquisition coverage and original units, reviewed mapping, saved editions, queries, comparison and an independently received operator workspace. Its proposal is $9,600 for 72 engineering hours over 12 active business days, with $4,800 at commencement and $4,800 at acceptance. First contact is prepared and unsent. The reusable native workflow has completed review, query/export, separate receiving and cold reopen on the publisher's illustrative observation; customer installation, live collection and the selected paid Stellar service are future work. The original workshare and product guide retain that scope.

The purchase targets must follow the selected buyers' work. Two buyers making one purchase on each ordinary weekday produce twenty purchases in fourteen consecutive days. Their T3 workorders must establish demand for at least thirty distinct useful paid requests across those same two buyers and both merchants. Additional purchases must correspond to agreed new periods, useful queries or the advertised pages and files needed for their tasks. The paid unit is defined before purchase; two paid pages can complete one task. Reopening, replay and cached use retain the original purchase. Work from another buyer is evaluated in its own cohort.

The shipped Customer-use Calendar saves those buyers, complete tasks, source periods and purchase or prepaid funding groups in the original Installation. It compares the schedule with the cohort target, associates actual purchase records and preserves later edits as new editions. This is the operating link between the workorder and the funded milestones.

TokenJunkieLabs earns defined implementation fees and separately scoped care. Merchants retain resource receipts; implementation partners retain customer relationships. Each workshare retains its effort, corrections, support period, customer acceptance and actual collections.

IATI customer operating procedure. A recurring publisher review also needs instructions another analyst can use. The installed IATI workflow turns an exact saved document-evidence edition into an editable Operating Plans procedure with the customer, owner, reporting period, ordered work and receiving destination. Its complete package carries the original case and saved plan history into the next analyst's application.

Why Stellar and what we contribute

Stellar provides native authorization and settlement for the reviewed purchase. In the x402 Exact flow, a buyer signs a Soroban token-transfer authorization binding payer, recipient, atomic amount and expiration. A facilitator submits it on the selected network; fee sponsorship can cover the transaction fee. Our implementation uses existing SDKs and token contracts.

The application retains the endpoint and method or MCP tool and arguments, request identity, selected source, payment option, complete output and fulfillment history. It checks the approved operation before dispatch and joins those records to the original native transaction. Wallet authority and aggregate spending remain with the buyer; source, pricing and fulfillment authority remain with the merchant.

Stellar's x402 CLI guide already covers the challenge, signed retry, returned response and transfer confirmation, including saving the full returned body when a further request incurs another payment. x402 facilitators supply verification and settlement; Bazaar supplies discoverable resource schemas. Existing ApiCharge and MPP Router provide typed paid access, discovery and retained request behavior.

Our Open Track contribution carries these foundations through the complete recurring customer task: reviewed source and query, aggregate approval, all agreed pages and files, editable customer output, unfinished-delivery recovery and merchant/accounting handover. The six packages deploy that workflow across independent merchants, buyers and facilitators, then publish the resulting source and receiving improvements. Native purchases, returning buyers and useful tasks another engineer can continue measure the value delivered to Stellar. The architecture and ecosystem comparison retains the detailed comparison.

Defined architecture and operating behavior

Six connected components carry the customer task from source selection to maintainable operation:

ComponentRetained operating responsibility
Merchant workspaceA private operator selects an authorized source edition or named query, schema, output and limits. Source or terms changes become separately reviewed states.
HTTP or MCP resourceAdapters preserve types, nulls, pagination, keys, units, time basis and snapshot/live behavior. Customer-controlled credential references govern source access.
Buyer approval and budgetThe buyer approves the exact method or tool, arguments, source scope and payment option. The original challenge and remote schema must match before signing. Per-payment limits and the existing budget reservation govern aggregate spending.
Stellar settlementThe native signer and facilitator use the reviewed network, asset, recipient, amount, expiry and fee policy. Independent RPC reconciliation checks the transfer. The existing MPP Charge integration retains its own challenge and recovery lifecycle.
Complete delivery and accountingThe application retains all agreed pages/files, original attempts, accepted output, merchant notification and acknowledgment. A prepaid request retains its selected pass and consumed allowance after defaults change. Pricing retains quantity, period, tariff and supplier-cost basis beside its invoice or service record.
Recovery and receivingConfirmation, transfer, output and fulfillment keep separate states. An uncertain response is reconciled through its original dispatch. Another engineer restores configuration, history and customer files, supplies authorized secret references and continues the work.

Catalog selection remains connected to execution. The buyer retains each complete original catalog page, selected row and payment alternative. Browse and search continuations preserve filters and coverage. Declared HTTP path/query fields or MCP arguments guide explicit input; a path template becomes a concrete URL under the configured merchant route, while advertised fixed values stay fixed. The native workflow saves that exact request, body and spending limit in its durable intent. Reopening status, recovery and output selects the same service workspace; complete downloads retain byte count and hash. The buyer discovery and native request package supplies this foundation.

Recurring service also has an operating close. The merchant connects prepaid orders to customers, retains usage captures and chooses opening and closing records for a period. Reviewed statements, saved closing cycles, corrections and complete customer handovers retain those original records. Purchase amounts, service activity and separately issued invoices stay available in their respective financial records.

Node.js implements browser, CLI, typed-client and MCP interfaces. Source and receiving applications also use Python/SQLite and PHP/WordPress/WooCommerce. The scope builds on existing Stellar SDKs and contracts. Each facilitator has explicit network, asset, recipient, signing-account and fee policies. T2 configures the same useful service for two compatible testnet operators; T3 deploys both merchants' reviewed mainnet configurations. The native signer and facilitator guide describes that operating foundation.

Working product and demonstrated results

Complete recurring-data operation — October 12, 2026. The OData product carried all 830 Orders from the original public reference source through typed collection, saved SQL, a report, a two-sheet workbook and independent analytical receiving. Its comparison operation preserved 830 matching keys and 4,150 field-selection differences, separately from value or null changes. The subsequent subscription operation completed baseline and incremental receiving, original-request replay, independent publisher/customer backup restores, restored-publisher continuation and customer edition 3. On the shared source definition, all 830 rows remained unchanged: zero added, removed, changed or event rows. Independent Analysis imported, exported, restored and queried all 830 rows. This establishes complete delivery and recovery behavior on the retained original source; the unchanged continuation supplies no new paid-customer or market-demand count. Collection result · Comparison result · Completed subscription result.

The customer edition carries 2,096 verified members, including 1,455 complete source files, the original and received workspaces, three subscription transfers, selected backups, analytical source, operation history and the usable subscription connection. Separately, the original managed-runtime selection built 3,884 source files / 54,966,117 bytes, and all twelve selected entry points loaded on Node 24.19.0 against the retained dependency graph. The source build is complete. Runtime preparation/adoption and managed Review → Start → download/restore → Stop → reopen remain the next operation on that already completed customer edition. The grant therefore has an operated native foundation and a published, fully supplied managed receiving programme, with installation-specific work and its observed outcome still to deliver. Build result · Same-operation receiving handoff.

The installation path is also present. Product Plans connects a complete customer capability selection to its immutable source recipe, dependency manifests, original native build and saved Runtime handoff. Request Collections turns original provider listings, payment alternatives and buyer operators into recurring request plans and named periods, then continues them through approval, payment and complete receiving.

Merchant operations continue after purchase. The bank application and handover joins OFX/QFX/CSV statements to original receipts, invoices and refunds, with gross receipts, separate fees, source corrections, remittance allocations and complete account close. The customer workbench carries profiles, orders and native usage through reviewed statements, saved closing cycles, corrections and grouped customer handovers. Browser, typed client and MCP retain the same operating records.

Discovery has an operated functional baseline. On October 12, 2026, we captured all 27 HTTP GET resources in the published Vellar testnet catalog, one 45,753-byte page whose returned total matched the rows. Actual ranking and index functions ran in V8 against those bytes. Twenty-four queries derived from published parameter names/descriptions yielded 31 declared query-resource relationships; nine retained general queries brought the full comparison to 33 queries. Schema-aware ranking found 31 of the 31 declared relationships, compared with 22 previously; 29 appeared in the first three results, compared with 19. Eleven positions improved and the rest were unchanged. Direct and indexed results matched for all 33 queries. This measures retrieval from published declarations. The captured catalog, complete comparison and maintained replay method accompany the application.

The source-adapter foundation includes an economic briefing with original observations and offline receiving; the merged 33-file Timescale integration, from commissioning source through immutable editions and analytical receiving; completed IATI organisation/programme finance and its original two-document native/SDK/Merchant/browser/receiving case; institutional-repository source and receiving work using an MSU journal edition and eleven selected staff cases; and company research whose Foundation and Singapore branch completed installed operation. The product and finance companion retains each full source population, operating result and current customer-deployment status.

A selected building-data integrator can use the Haystack workflow to review original point lists and publish an agreed model/report edition or native-validation service. Its buyer approves the Stellar purchase and receives every advertised file with original point identities, dictionary and contractor-return history. The modelling, contractor-return and installed-interface source is merged. Actual offline Brick 1.4.4 installation, ontology catalogue and eight-row CSV inspection completed; the interrupted validator returned no conformance report, and the full native/browser programme remains to be operated. This foundation supplies a possible customer-specific deployment through the same T1 source/receiving, T2 provider/response and T3 mainnet/recovery packages.

These completed capabilities establish the starting point for the grant: acquire the agreed resource, use it in the customer's application, retain its commercial history, and let another engineer continue the original work. The selected installations' remaining source, authority, network, recurring-use and receiving gaps determine the work within the six funded packages.

Implemented IATI procedure and handover. The merged customer operating procedure joins the original document case to editable Operating Plans, the installed CLI and typed SDK. The customer can retain the selected source, catalog, ordered work and complete plan revisions, then export Markdown/HTML and receive the full package. The original IATI ZIP supplies the native workspace and acquired document bytes.

Delivery responsibility and receiving

Bryce remains accountable for the complete award. Each installation workorder assigns the following human responsibilities before its deployed work begins; one person may hold several roles, but the two merchant and two buyer independence requirements apply to their accountable organizations or people across wallets and agents.

ResponsibilityRequired contribution and decision
Bryce / project leadSelect the two delivery workorders, allocate the 400 hours once, maintain source and release ownership, submit tranche outcomes and reconcile contributor commitments with commercial work.
Integration engineerImplement the chosen source, merchant and consuming-application changes; deliver the source/profile selection, dependency lock, configuration and completed operating records.
Merchant operator / source ownerAuthorize source access and publication rights; approve source meaning, price, network, asset, recipient, release or withdrawal, and the host's ongoing service costs.
Independent buyer operatorApprove the complete useful task, its request, total spending and receiving application; retain the original purchase and assess whether the agreed output is usable.
Receiving engineer / support ownerRestore the complete delivered edition in separate authorized paths, configure the actual host and secret references, continue the original operation and record the change/recovery and support result.
Named acceptance ownerReview the agreed source and full output, compare the observed outcome with the workorder, and record acceptance or the specific remaining correction.

For a recurring-data installation, the recipient inspects the original source selection, receives publisher and customer backups, opens the complete rows and saved report, reviews the current edition through the selected application, then downloads and independently restores its complete output. The operator stops and reopens the same managed service and confirms that the selected connection, original requests and earlier delivered editions remain available. A later edition is assessed against the same keys, fields and population; a genuine no-change result remains no change. This receiving path is part of the existing technical integration/handover hours.

T1 ends with both installed services and the second-operator change by day 30. T2's seven-day use window and installed response cases finish by day 90. T3's fourteen-day mainnet window, return use and production receiving finish by day 150. The delivery dates are measured from actual award acceptance; each completion submission also follows its separate 90-day clock from the preceding actual SCF payment.

Remaining work after the completed OData operation. The original source capture, 830-row analytical receiving, comparison, three subscription editions, complete customer package, managed source build and entry-point imports are pre-award work. The six packages fund the selected customers' remaining access and source mappings, deployed Stellar pricing/payment and consumer joins, installed response controls, mainnet release and independent operating handover. Runtime adoption and managed receiving of the current supplied edition still have an unstarted outcome; completion before award reduces the corresponding remaining implementation rather than becoming reimbursable past work. The same review is applied to any selected customer product.

Threat response and outcome measurement

T2 includes a documented threat model, the corresponding installed monitoring plan and material corrections. Each installation records its source edition, authority, network, facilitator, protected records, observations, thresholds, notification destinations and primary/backup responders. Threats include changed offers or approvals, wrong payment/output attribution, unauthorized access, interrupted delivery, missing observations and restoring the wrong generation. Each connects to an observable signal, monitor, accountable responder and recovery action. Source and fulfillment failures receive application-level observation. The implementation follows Stellar's threat-modeling guidance and builder monitoring template.

The customer operates both an interrupted settled purchase and a merchant-delivery failure. The original incident retains financial and delivery states, notification and acknowledgment, response/recovery times and useful output. The receiving engineer reopens it after restart, including any observation gaps.

A completed purchase requires one distinct approved intent, an independently observed native transfer and complete useful output. Transactions are deduplicated per network; assets and fees remain separate. A prepaid pass counts once when its first agreed operation produces accepted complete output, with later calls retained as usage. A customer task completes only when every agreed page, file and required order action is accepted. The HPD example is therefore two purchases and one complete task.

The T2 target is ten purchases across two independent buyers in seven consecutive days; T3 is thirty in fourteen consecutive days, with both buyers returning on another UTC day. Both merchants must receive independent use. Independence follows the accountable person or organization across its agents and wallets.

The original first attempt determines cohort membership. Settlement and accepted complete output must fall within the selected window; later observations retain their actual time. Attempted, completed, partial, unresolved, canceled and refunded outcomes all remain in the cohort. Comparison across the two facilitators holds the service, schema, population and output constant.

Customer benefit compares the prior task, first installed execution and recurring use on the same population or period: active effort, manual corrections, time to accepted output and unresolved work. For a stated period, direct labor value uses completed tasks, comparable active hours saved and the customer's stated hourly value, then subtracts implementation and incremental provider, hosting, payment and support costs. The workorder retains these inputs beside accepted milestones, fees, collections and actual support effort.

A transfer that settled before an interrupted response is recovered through its original entitlement or delivery session. An uncertain transfer is reconciled before any further financial action.

The acceptance report includes the actual installation coverage and unresolved findings with the two original recovery cases. Public grant reporting uses the outcome counts, timings and sanitized source/version references; request bodies, account credentials, customer files and populated response destinations remain in the operator’s protected workspace.

Delivery capacity, payment timing and sustainability

Bryce allocates contributors and operating resources to the six packages. The retained 400-hour/150-day model's lowest examined timely allocation is 25 engineering hours plus eight technical integration/handover hours per week. This is modeled capacity; named contributor availability and payment arrangements are being finalized against the actual award date. Grant and accepted commercial work use one calendar, allocating each contributor's available hours once.

The current commercial-capacity study joins five complete proposed workshares—Freeform, Lutra, CoCart, Query.Farm and Zeeve—totaling 320 hours and $40,320 in fees. It preserves original phases, invoice terms, delivery windows and included support. At the stated $95/hour allocation and proposed CoCart referral, they contribute $9,560 before further costs, or $3,480 with 20% more customer effort.

Its dated planning sequence starts Freeform on October 13, Lutra on October 29 and CoCart on November 16 on a core engineering role; Query.Farm starts October 13 and Zeeve November 4 on an additional role. Two entered 30-hour/week roles carry that pre-award sequence, then the original grant capacity returns to 25 engineering plus eight integration hours per week. All 33 modeled tasks across the grant packages and customer phases meet their selected windows; the modeled grant finishes April 13 from the assumed December 7 award. Customer starts depend on their original readiness and commencement conditions. Actual agreements, named availability and collections populate the existing Forecast and Portfolio.

Under those dated inputs, commercial delivery requires $3,259 of interim funding before the assumed award. A further fourteen-day delay to post-start customer collections raises that requirement to $10,960.67. The main case reduces the fourteen-day-lag grant programme's peak requirement from $17,250 to $7,690. These are scenario results using proposed workshares and collections. The complete study retains all original closures, eight alternatives, workload sensitivity and 14/30/60-day grant lags. Actual cash balances and agreed payment dates replace the entered assumptions as they become known.

The separate GeoRobotix proposal requires 72 engineering hours over twelve active business days, six hours per active day or thirty in a five-day week. It cannot use the same hours already allocated to the grant. Its selected schedule must provide actual additional capacity or a nonconflicting delivery window. Proposed $4,800 commencement and acceptance receipts remain uncollected scenario inputs. Customer access or approval delays change the active-day schedule through the agreed workorder.

SCF's four award payments are $3,800 at acceptance, then $7,600, $11,400 and $15,200 after the respective deliverables are approved under the Build payment schedule. Delivery costs by tranche are $11,400, $11,400 and $15,200. The USD-equivalent award is paid in XLM at CF XLMUSD_RR or SDF's qualifying alternative on the actual payment day under the Official Rules.

The retained grant-only sensitivity assumes the full package value is paid in cash over scheduled work dates, with no entered opening balance. Peak interim funding under that assumption is $17,250 at a fourteen-day review/payment lag, $23,275 at thirty days and $26,600 at sixty days. The Operating Forecast instead allows the actual opening balance, remaining cash estimates, agreed contributor/vendor dates, original unpaid invoices and observed receipts. Work and invoice intake connects reviewed source rows to the funded packages and actual obligations.

Each tranche completion form is due within 90 calendar days of the preceding actual payment. An anticipated delay requires SDF's written acknowledgment before the original deadline and a confirmed revised date. The Delivery calendar retains original deadlines, confirmed extensions, contributor assignments and planned submissions, with full iCalendar/CSV/JSON receiving. Actual receipts determine those deadlines; forecast dates support the cash model.

Sustainability comes from customer-specific implementation and separately scoped care around the reusable open-source product. Completed reusable work reduces the remaining prospective grant estimate at award. Accepted scope, each contributor's time and each adaptation's cost are assigned once across the grant and commercial workshares; original milestones, collections, corrections and support responsibilities remain in the same operating case.

Maintainable release and support handover

The day-150 handover gives each independent operator one source-versioned release, its saved product plan and original installed Runtime handoff, dependency and license inventory, installation and upgrade instructions, selected configuration references, and the original customer data/state receiving procedure. The product briefing identifies that same selected installation and its observed package versions; the complete plan and original receiving records carry the source and operating state. It also names the host owner, maintainer, primary and backup responder, service-cost owner and separately agreed care scope. These are deliverables of the existing rollout and recovery packages.

The installed grant reviewer can turn the selected native SF47 work packages into a named customer operating procedure. It carries the original package scope, price, hours, relative work window and completion measure into ordered, editable steps; selected toolkit commands retain their source and runtime declarations. The receiving engineer adds the installation-specific instructions, actual due dates and recorded results in Operating plans. Complete saved revisions and readable HTML or Markdown carry that working procedure to the next operator alongside the original planning file.

Updates begin from the deployed source and preserve the merchant’s public resource identity, buyer records and state directories outside the installed package. The operator reviews changed routes, schemas and payment terms, stages the replacement and drains admitted work before switching traffic. A rollback selects a retained release while preserving later purchases and fulfilled output. A receiving-host restore reconciles operations after the backup point before continuing unfinished work.

During funded delivery, dependency or protocol changes are assessed against the selected Stellar SDK, x402 wire format, token/account behavior and the installations that use them. Necessary compatibility corrections return to the maintained source with the affected operating example and migration instructions. The selected provider’s sponsored-fee declaration, authorization lifetime, accepted payment flow and transaction payload remain explicit parts of that compatibility review.

At handover, the maintainer receives known limitations, open support cases and the continuation procedure for each one. The installed release and usable customer output remain available for self-operation. Paid care is separately scoped around the actual hosting, response and upgrade responsibilities; the grant’s 400 hours and $38,000 fund the prospective six-package delivery described here.
